hard_rule_findings.title: Current delivered execution bytes are not tied to the passed root source

rule.text: Verify declared artifacts against manifests and committed delivery blobs; check runtime source against its recorded execution revision.

hard_rule_findings.protocol: 39b-fresh-delivery-protocol-01 requires captured runtime/tool/input identities and exact609 root acceptance for its declared4f80 execution source.
hard_rule_findings.impact: The loop proves captured records match their historical commits. It never proves the current delivery's source/test/config/tool set and bytes match the root source-manifest-before. A post-root code change plus rebuilt global delivery manifest can pass all current checks while shipping an unregressed implementation. Current protected-scope check omits src/tests/scripts.
hard_rule_findings.requested_change: Bind execution_source to its protocol/authority; require the passed-root source manifest to equal its committed execution set, then require current runtime/tests/configs/execution tools to match that set and bytes. Permit only the explicitly declared new saved-only verifier or other nonexecution additions, not arbitrary extra source paths.
hard_rule_findings.counterexample: Static only: change a runtime Python file after4f80, add its new Git hash to the global delivery manifest, leave historical root source receipts intact. Current code compares each side to its own Git revision and never compares the delivered runtime to the regressed runtime.

hard_rule_findings.title: Nested captured/native datasets can be omitted while the global delivery remains complete

rule.text: Define the durable input/output set before hashing, preserve immutable originals and validate the declared delivery without arbitrary omissions.

hard_rule_findings.protocol: Fresh protocol requires all captured runtime/tool/input identities and remote native hashes with complete JSON/JSONL readability; it excludes no original native member.
hard_rule_findings.impact: files dictionaries inside captured source manifests and private-raw-index are iterated without original start/terminal hash or exact-set binding. A private index can be empty or omit one trace file and no check fails. JSONL zero lines also pass. The independent review-originals-manifest has original SHA values but is never consumed, so global hashes alone cannot establish original reviewer-byte retention after reindexing.
hard_rule_findings.requested_change: Require nonempty dictionaries. Bind staged source manifests to attempt.manifest_sha256 and source identities; bind root before-manifests to original terminal output hashes. Bind every private index to the corresponding terminal.output_files exact nonempty native set/bytes/SHA, not just a positive count. Require nonempty native JSONL and verify the original-review SHA index. Enforce resolved namespace containment for private staging inputs as already done for native files.
hard_rule_findings.concrete_existing_link: slice04 terminal.output_files contains exactly the same cases/.../actual-run scenario.json/private-state.jsonl/balances.jsonl/run.json paths and hashes as its private-raw-index; this supplies an existing immutable reference without scientific recomputation.
hard_rule_findings.namespace_detail: For source-objects.pack/execution-snapshot.json, Path(attempt).name==attempt accepts '..' and no resolved containment is checked before REMOTE/attempt access. Reject this path escape within the same private-input binding fix.
hard_rule_findings.counterexample: Static only: remove one or all private index entries and rehash that JSON in the global manifest; other source references remain, so the verifier can report PASS with the omitted native data never opened. Or delete one staged source entry while the original attempt still records the old manifest SHA; that mismatch is currently unchecked.
